newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Helix says more gold signs from Gawler.
newsitem.headline: Helix says more gold signs from Gawler.

text.p: Helix Resources NL said drilling in the Gawler Craton region of South Australia had defined further gold mineralisation at its key Area 223 site and further north.
Helix said additional drilling at Area 223, located in the southern portion of the western demagnetised zone (WDZ), suggested that high-grade plunging ore shoots are possible.
It said the drilling indicated that strong mineralisation extended to a vertical depth of about 200 metres before easing between 200 and 250 metres.

Helix also said in its June quarter report that drilling in the WDZ had recovered grades varying between 0.4 grams per tonne (g/t) gold and 2.0 g/t for a distance of four km north of Area 223 within the overall Tunkillia anomaly.

"Whilst the overall gold grade averages around 0.8 g/t gold in the WDZ, the company is delighted with the extent of the gold mineralised system and our technical team believes it is almost certainly related to a nearby larger gold rich resource," it said.

"Further exploration activities related to finding the source as well as direct investigations on the potential economic implications of the low grade WDZ will be carried out during the next six months."
The share market fortunes of Helix and other Gawler explorers have slumped in recent months after investors and analysts had focussed on Gawler as posssibly Australia's next big gold region.
Helix shares were 10 cents lower at 85 cents at 1.30 p.m. (0330 GMT).

Its stock reached a record high of A$4.99 earlier in 1997 when the Gawler euphoria was at a peak and just before major gold miner Acacia Resources Ltd AA.AX acquired a 17.4 percent stake in February at an average price of A$4.20.
Acacia raised its stake to the takeover threshold of 19.9 percent in April but said earlier on Thursday that it was now reconsidering its investment.
